what: M7 fleet simulation (docs/M7-FLEET.md): 10,000 tenants registered, written to, and slept on one mutinyd; resident memory measured while they sleep; a random subset of 200 receives deltas and wakes selectively (resident count asserted == woken count); wake-to-first-answer = one waking write + the first standing-SQL read, timed end-to-end through the HTTP door.

run.host: Apple Silicon macOS (Darwin 24.6.0), local development machine
run.memory_ceiling: none on this host — the CI job that repeats this run (nightly.yml fleet-sim-10k) executes under a systemd-run cgroup with MemoryMax=2G, MemorySwapMax=0; the 1.5 GiB in-test budget is asserted in both

read_the_conditions: These are same-host, local-disk numbers and claim nothing about wide-area wake. The wide-area story lives on the component track (substrate get_batch + WarmPool, ~1 RTT median measured against Sydney at RTT~226ms) and is inherited, not re-measured here — see README 'Wake latency, honestly'. The per-sleeper resident cost is dominated by the registry row (full TenantConfig) plus allocator retention from registry serialization churn; the registry file itself is O(fleet) and rewritten atomically per state change, which is also why build_secs grows superlinearly and is not a gated number.
